history.content: My React application using the App Configuration React client SDK is not connecting to the App Configuration service instance despite correct initialization. How can I get this fixed?

Here are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot the issue: 1. **Check your internet connection**: Ensure that your React application has a stable internet connection, as the App Configuration React client SDK needs to connect to the App Configuration service instance. 2. **Verify the initialization parameters**: Double-check the region, guid, apikey, collectionId, and environmentId values you're using for initialization. Make sure they are correct and match the ones in your App Configuration service instance. 3. **Check if the App Configuration SDK handles the automatic delivery of the appropriate flag state or property value into your application from the App Configuration instance. 4. **Create service credentials for Client SDK**: Ensure that you have created the service credentials of the role Client SDK for use with the React client SDK. 5. **Test the connection**: Check if the various metrics are sent back to the AC cloud service and the service is operating properly so that you can monitor its operation. If you've tried these steps and the issue persists, I would recommend reaching out to IBM support with detailed information about the problem, including any error messages and steps taken to resolve the issue.
What are the different types of SDKs available and why is it necessary for services offering public APIs to also offer SDKs?

There are three main types of SDKs available for App Configuration: Server-side SDKs, Client-side SDKs, and Admin SDKs. Server-side SDKs are designed for multi-user systems and are intended to be used in trusted environments, such as inside a corporate network or on a web server. Client-side SDKs are meant for use in web and mobile applications and are designed to handle the automatic delivery of the appropriate flag state or property value into your application. The Admin SDK is designed to perform App Configuration service instance management and is used to create and manage configurations for Environments, Collections, Feature flags, Properties, and Segments from within your application. The Server-side SDKs connect to the App Configuration service through a web socket for real-time updates, while the Client-side SDKs pull values from the App Configuration service upon a lifecycle change such as being opened or brought to the foreground. SDKs are available in various client-side and serve-side languages, with more languages being added all the time. It is necessary for services offering public APIs to also offer SDKs because SDKs provide a basic interface that maps directly onto the operations of the underlying API, making it easier for developers to interact with the service. SDKs also handle various tasks like streaming, asynchronous method calls, and instrumentation, allowing developers to focus on building their applications instead of dealing with low-level implementation details.
How can one ensure that the application and SDK continue working even during an App Configuration service downtime?

To ensure that the application and SDK continue working even during an App Configuration service downtime, you can configure the SDK to work by using a persistent cache. This allows the SDK to store the App Configuration data that is available across your application restarts. When a persistent cache is enabled, the SDK keeps the last known good configuration at the persistent cache. If the App Configuration server is unreachable, the latest configurations at the persistent cache are loaded to the application to continue working. It's important to ensure that the cache file is not lost or deleted, for example, by storing it in a persistent volume by providing the correct absolute path of the persistent directory. Additionally, the SDK is designed to serve configurations and perform feature flag and property evaluations without being connected to the App Configuration service even when offline.

See the best practice [Use only services that are IBM Cloud for Financial Services Validated](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/framework-financial-services?topic=framework-financial-services-best-practicesbest-practices-financial-services-validated-services) for more details and potential exceptions.





 What if I don't want to use managed services, but I want to install and manage my own software? 

Self-installed (or "bring your own") software from third parties is permitted without special approval. Examples include databases, logging stacks, web application firewalls, and so on. But just like first-party software you might develop and deploy, self-installed third-party software must comply with all of the requirements of the IBM Cloud Framework for Financial Services. And, it is your responsibility to provide appropriate supporting evidence.

For more information, see [Ensure all usage of software meets IBM Cloud Framework for Financial Services controls](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/framework-financial-services?topic=framework-financial-services-best-practicesbest-practices-self-installed-software).

[Getting started](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/text-to-speech?topic=text-to-speech-gettingStarted) offers examples of both the HTTP POST /v1/synthesize and GET /v1/synthesize methods. The [API & SDK reference](https://cloud.ibm.com/apidocs/text-to-speech) shows examples of all interfaces and methods.

There is no graphical user interface for submitting text. See the [Text to Speech demo](https://www.ibm.com/demos/live/tts-demo/self-service/home) to try an example of the service in action. The demo accepts a small amount of your text as input to generate speech with different voices.
* Can I change how the service interprets input text and produces synthesized audio?

You can use the Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) to control aspects of the synthesis process such as pronunciation, volume, pitch, speed, and other attributes. You can also use the Tune by Example feature to tailor the prosody, intonation, and cadence of custom prompts to better suit your application needs.
